note: Seat-axis violations tolerated as of v1.145.0 (2026-08-27), each named per CLAUDE.md 6.7 — an aggregate count is unfalsifiable and rots into permanent noise. S1 = a card served to both seats of one site. S2 = a seat that owns no card of its own, so _blend_deck hands it the role-agnostic tier and both seats read identically. S4 = one submission family authored as finishing from both seats of one position. Shrinking this list always passes; a row that has been fixed is reported so it can be deleted in the same commit. Regenerate: python3 scripts/validate_seat_decks.py --baseline (then restore the reasons). Inspect: python3 scripts/validate_seat_decks.py --report

reviewed.Kimura Trap/Americana (general rule, 202: decided_by: owner_decision (general rule, 2026-09-01). The owner generalised the Kimura Trap seat ruling: 'each seat gets its own true content; a finish is dealable from the seat that actually holds the lock.' `Americana from Kimura Trap` re-seated Top -> Bottom under it. This is the one pair in the whole corpus where the rule applies MECHANICALLY rather than requiring a fresh ontology call, because the seat question was already settled by the v1.157.0 ruling and the Americana is a DEPENDENT of the same grip by its own authored text: 'The figure-four grip is already established, so you change the direction of force rather than reconfiguring your hands.' Leaving it on Top put the same figure four in both players' hands — the defect one family sideways, where S4 cannot see it. PRICE, measured and accepted: 3 further value-dropping success cells (5 total against the pre-ruling graph) and V0 0.076847 -> 0.076437, because Kimura Trap/Top now has no finish at all. Recorded in tests/artifacts/flow_validation_baseline.json `reviewed`. In v1.157.0 this move was measured and HELD on exactly that cost; the owner's general rule supersedes the cost argument, and the correctness argument is unchanged.
reviewed.Kimura Trap/Kimura (owner ruling, v1.157: decided_by: owner_decision. OWNER RULING ON THIS ONE PAIR, superseding the hung P6b panel FOR KIMURA TRAP ONLY. SCOPE PIN, in the owner's words: the other opposite-seat pairs under P6b REMAIN HUNG and this must not be generalised to them — `S4:Omoplata Control/Omoplata` and `S1:Guillotine Control` are untouched and stay untouched. THE RULING: Kimura Trap/Bottom is the seat that actually holds the lock — the trapped-turned-attacker — so `Kimura from Kimura Trap` is dealt from Bottom, not Top. Before this, BOTH seats were authored as the grip holder (top.overview 'the top practitioner secures a Kimura grip'; bottom.overview 'the practitioner secures a Kimura grip'), which is one state playing both sides of its own exchange — the defect S4 exists to name. S4 never fired here because only one Kimura child existed at this position, so the position passed green while the data was wrong. IMPLEMENTED BY MOVING THE DATA, never by touching the gate: from_position, the failure and counter outcome seats, from_positions, and the attacker mechanics — which were authored as a TOP finish (chest pressure, walking the feet toward the head) and are now the bottom finish (leg entanglement as the anchor, hip-escape onto the near elbow for the angle). It is now that seat's biggest move at gi 21, which is what bottom.related_content has always promised: 'Kimura — Primary submission threat'. SCOPE HELD AT THE KIMURA, AND MEASURED. The agent first also moved `Americana from Kimura Trap`, on the grounds that its own text makes it a dependent of the same grip ('The figure-four grip is already established'). That was DROPPED after measurement: FLOW's content ratchet gives 2 new value-dropping success cells for the Kimura alone and 5 with the Americana too, and V0 0.076847 vs 0.076437. The owner's literal instruction measured strictly better, so the Americana stays on Top and its top-authored prose stays correct for it. THE PRICE, ratified with the ruling and carried in tests/artifacts/flow_validation_baseline.json: Kimura Trap/Top no longer finishes, so arriving there is worth less, and two success cells that feed it now drop value. That is the ruling being priced, not an authoring defect. STILL OPEN, deliberately untouched: Kimura Trap/Top still deals `North-South to Kimura` (gi 14) and `Kimura to Back Take` (gi 19), which are grip-HOLDER moves and are on the wrong seat under this same ruling. Re-homing the six grip-establishing success edges onto Bottom was MEASURED and is WORSE (3 new rows, V0 0.076542), because Bottom is a bottom position — so the fix is not a re-home, and it is a separate content decision. SEPARATE PRE-EXISTING DEFECT, found while re-seating and NOT created by it: twelve of the twenty-two attacker flashcards in this file are explicitly titled 'the Kimura from north-south' — a mis-filed block whose correct home, `Kimura/from North-South`, is one of the 27 family variations the hubs declare with no file behind them. They were already served from a Kimura Trap seat before this ruling, so they were left untouched rather than silently rewritten into invented content or deleted.
reviewed.S1:Guillotine Control: NOT the card-vs-graph mismatch it first reads as. The one shared card ('What is the primary escape your opponent will attempt and how do you shut it down?') is shared because BOTH seats are authored as the guillotine attacker, and that is defensible on its face: bottom.overview says 'the bottom practitioner has secured a guillotine choke grip while maintaining guard', which is a real position (guillotine from closed guard), and top is the front-headlock guillotine. The actual defect is the edge set: Guillotine Control/Bottom carries three moves authored FROM it — `Guillotine Escape via Posture`, `Guard Recovery from Guillotine Control` and `Guillotine Escape to Von Flue` — that belong to whoever is BEING choked. A Von Flue is the passer's counter. So one seat holds both sides of its own exchange, exactly as Omoplata Control does, and the repair is to re-home three edges, not to rewrite eight cards. Same class as S4, same reason to wait.
reviewed.S4:Omoplata Control/Omoplata: THE TRAPPED PLAYER HAS NO SEAT IN THIS FILE. `Omoplata from Omoplata Control` is authored from Top and `Rolling Omoplata from Omoplata Control` from Bottom, while the three escapes (Cartwheel, Roll Forward, Stack Defense) are also on Bottom — so Bottom both finishes and escapes the same submission. Every other field agrees with neither reading: both seats are typed Offensive, both seats' prerequisites describe the attacker ('Base has been established with the free leg to prevent being rolled forward'), all eight cards on each seat teach applying the omoplata, and ALL SIX machine-verified clips are attacker footage — top carries 'Omoplata finish with far leg control', bottom carries 'Spinning omoplata setup'. The clip list is the one field an LLM pass may not write, which is the standard the New York Control / Invisible Collar review set, and here it does not disambiguate: it convicts both seats. Deciding which seat becomes the victim is a seat assignment and commits the ontology, so it waits for P6b. Two further defects sit underneath and are NOT this row: Omoplata Control/Bottom lists `Omoplata Sweep` and `Triangle Setup`, both authored from Closed Guard/Bottom, so they are wrong-origin references that scripts/audit_from_position.py owns.
